scene_text: Rama reveals his Vishvarupa to Sati, his body containing suns, moons, gods, and countless beings radiating cosmic light.
The miraculous birth of Skanda—an infant with six radiant heads and twelve arms—appearing at dawn among sacred reeds while gods shower flowers from the heavens.
From a braid flung by Shiva onto a silver mountain, the monstrous warrior Virabhadra with a thousand arms arises beside the fierce goddess Bhadra Kali as Shiva’s hordes roar for battle.
Sati, in despair before the sacrificial altar, leaps into the blazing yajna fire while stunned sages and her father Daksha look on.
Sati, in serene yogic trance before the yajna altar, leaps into towering sacrificial flames as the stunned assembly watches.
Lord Rama reveals his vast cosmic Vishvarupa to Sati, his body containing suns, gods, and countless beings shining in divine light.
The radiant six‑headed infant Skanda appears at dawn in the darbha reeds as gods shower flowers from the sky.
Shiva tears a lock of his matted hair and hurls it to the ground, from which the fierce thousand‑armed warrior Virabhadra arises.
The divine seed of Siva passing through cosmic elements—Fire, Svaha, the White Mountain, the Ganges, and a jungle of reeds—each struggling to contain its blazing power.
Shiva opens his blazing third eye and a pillar of divine fire bursts forth, reducing the love-god Manmatha to ashes as the entire garden burns.
Shiva opens his blazing third eye and a column of fire burns Manmatha to ashes in the flowering Bilva garden.
The battlefield before Sonitapura where Skanda, mounted and blowing his conch, faces the vast demon armies of Taraka beneath a storm-dark sky.
Siva and Parvati arrive on the shining silver slopes of Mount Kailasa as gods, spirits, and celestial beings gather amid supernatural light to welcome the divine couple.
Skanda arriving at Mount Kailasa in the Pushpaka aircraft while gods shower flowers and celestial beings gather across the snowy peaks to welcome him.
The celestial wedding of Siva and Sati where gods, sages, and divine beings gather while heavenly flowers rain down and Siva’s serpents bow to the bride.
Nandanar enters the Chidambaram temple in a trance of devotion as a sacred flame rises at Nataraja’s feet and engulfs him in radiant light.
Parvati performs fierce penance among the five sacred fires under the blazing sun, dressed in simple bark cloth while gods watch the flames of her austerity rise skyward.
Parvati embracing the young Skanda before the assembled gods as milk miraculously flows from her in a radiant expression of divine motherhood.
Parvati descends from the sky beside young Jnana Sambandhi, nursing the child and gifting him a golden throne and royal emblems beneath a celestial glow.
Hidden behind a Bilva tree, Manmatha releases a flower-arrow toward the meditating Shiva as spring blossoms and birds awaken around them.
Skanda fires the blazing Agneya weapon that shatters the Siva-idol pendant on Taraka’s neck into five flaming fragments.
In a grand wedding hall, Shiva and Sati sit on a golden plank as priests chant and heavenly beings shower flower petals from above.
Lord Shiva in disguise sits before a meal prepared from Siriyala’s sacrificed son, only to restore the boy to life as the stunned parents fall at the deity’s feet.
Inside the temple, a sacred flame at Nataraja’s feet suddenly flares up and engulfs the radiant Nandanar as astonished priests watch.
In the flowering Bilva garden, Manmatha hides behind a tree and releases glowing flower-arrows toward the meditating Shiva while spring erupts around the forest.
Goddess Durga leaps onto the buffalo-demon Mahishasura, pinning him beneath her feet while thrusting a spear into his body.
Skanda stands on the battlefield blowing his conch while his vast celestial army surrounds Taraka’s city of Sonitapura.
Daksha standing in the sacrificial assembly angrily denouncing Siva before Brahma, Vishnu, sages, and stunned gods.
The goddess Parvati descends from the sky, cradling and nursing a small boy on the riverbank while celestial gifts appear around him.
The hunter Tinnadu plucks out his own eye and presses it onto the bleeding eye of the Siva idol in desperate devotion.
At Taraka’s birth the earth quakes, storms rage, stars fall, and terrified animals scatter under a darkened sky.
On Mount Kailasa, Shiva and Parvati dance joyfully among peacocks as the silver mountain glows with supernatural light.
Princess Srimati walks past the monkey-faced Narada and places her wedding garland on Vishnu disguised as a radiant prince in the royal court.
The Shiva linga cracks open in a burst of light as the three‑eyed Shiva emerges angrily with his trident to confront the god of death.
Parvati, stripped of royal ornaments, walks toward the forest in simple bark cloth while her grieving parents watch with tears.
Sati kneels with tears of ecstasy touching Shiva’s feet while the ash‑smeared god with matted hair smiles gently at her devotion.
